name: stet
what: The copy layer for everything you ship: every string is a typed key, edited by whoever writes the words and published without a build, while a complete copy stays committed in your repo.
glance: Site copy, transactional email, broadcasts, contacts, SEO fields and agent text
A hosted dashboard, the editor mounted in your own app, the CLI, or an agent over MCP
In seconds, with no rebuild and no deploy
Apache-2.0 self-hosted — Cloud sells hosting, review and custody
archHi:
stet is the copy layer for everything you ship. Every sentence a product says — website copy, transactional email, bot messages, SEO fields — lives behind a typed key instead of being hard-coded in a component.

  1. Install. One command detects the framework and the store, writes the registry, and leaves the first key rendering. Copy already sitting in your components can be adopted where it is.
  2. The people who write the words edit them. Marketers, editors, clients and AI agents all work on copy directly, and none of them touches structure, layout or code.
  3. Changes go live in seconds. No rebuild, no deploy, and no developer in the loop.

Everyone works where they already are:

WhoWhere they work
Editors and marketersa hosted dashboard, or the editor mounted straight into your own app — your login, your theme
Clients and reviewersa signed preview link that shows the change in place, with no account and no seat
Developersthe CLI, in the terminal alongside everything else
AI agentsMCP — Claude or any agent, held behind an approval wall or allowed to publish

A complete copy of every string stays committed in your repo, so a missing value or an unreachable database renders the shipped default rather than a blank page. Self-hosting is the whole mechanism under Apache-2.0; stet Cloud adds the hosted workspace, approvals, scheduling, sending and contact custody on top.
arch:
Coding agents made shipping a site cheap. Keeping one current never got cheaper: every wording change, SEO fix or new email means opening that project, rebuilding an agent's context from scratch, burning tokens to rediscover a codebase it has seen a dozen times, and shipping a deploy — once per property. The words are the thing you change most often and the most expensive thing to change.

stet takes them out of the code without handing them to a content system. Every string is a typed key with a complete copy committed in your repo, and the live value is edited on top of that copy — so the compiler still knows the copy exists, the repo still holds it, and nobody waits for a deploy. One workspace covers every site and app you run, which turns an improvement like a new SEO rule into a package update that lands everywhere at once instead of a project per property.

That shape decides the rest of the architecture:

  • Keys are typed, so mistakes surface at compile time. Keys generate into the host's types — an unknown key is a build error rather than a blank space in production.
  • Values are immutable. A revert mints a new row instead of editing one, so history is never lost and a publish is a transaction rather than a build.
  • The committed snapshot is the floor. Every read falls through to it, so an absent value or an unreachable store degrades to the last shipped wording instead of failing the page.
  • Four stores, one conformance suite. Snapshot-only, plain Postgres and hosted all implement the same port — “no database at all” and “our Postgres” are the same code path to the caller.

Cloud is split into three tiers by what downtime actually costs:

TierRuns onWhat lives there
T1 — always upsomeone else's edgecontent reads, form and unsubscribe endpoints, click redirects, campaign archive
T2 — working hoursone app deploymentdashboard, editor, API, auth, review, billing
T3 — catches upqueued jobsbundle materialisation, mirror commits, scheduled publishes, sends, exports
  • The read path never touches the app. A publish materialises an immutable versioned bundle to object storage and flips a version pointer; sites read edge → token check → immutable object. There is no cache to purge and no origin to overload.
  • Nothing sits between the edge and durable storage. Form and unsubscribe events land in a durable queue in milliseconds and survive an app or database outage entirely; a consumer drains them on recovery.
  • The repo is a mirror, not a dependency. After each publish a GitHub App commits the snapshot back to the customer's repository, opening a pull request where the branch is protected.
  • Email is copy too. Message text lives as named slots on the customer's own template, marketing sends are blocked until an unsubscribe link is in scope, and the send ledger claims each recipient inside the batch transaction — a retry can never double-send.
  • Contacts stay where custody belongs. Self-hosted, subscriber rows never leave the customer's own Postgres. Hosted, they sit behind a processor agreement with per-subscriber export and deletion the customer runs themselves.
proc:
• One core, three front doors. A single TypeScript package serves a developer's build step, an editor's browser and an agent's tool call — CLI, MCP server and React components over the same operations, with an Astro marketing site on top.
  • Ports and adapters, proved by conformance. Every store implements one port and passes a single conformance suite, so a new backend is an adapter and a test run, never a fork of the read path.
  • Safe-to-fail is an architectural constraint. Work is placed by what its downtime costs: the tier that cannot fail runs entirely on someone else's edge, and everything operated in-house recovers by retrying. Nothing pages anyone at night, by construction.
  • Bought, not built. Certificates, bot defence, image transforms, cron durability, auth and payments are all vendors. The count of things actually operated is one app deployment.
  • Exits are declared before they're needed. Each metered vendor carries the threshold at which it stops making sense and the platform it ports to, so a migration is a scheduled decision rather than an incident.
  • The docs are the source, not a description. The published sub-processor page is derived from the service inventory, so a vendor added in code is a line added to a legal document.
  • The product is its own first customer. stet's own site renders from stet — and still renders with stet switched off.
